newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Arab group asks U.N. to halt Israeli settlements.
newsitem.headline: Arab group asks U.N. to halt Israeli settlements.

text.p: The Arab group at the United Nations complained in letters circulated on Tuesday over Israeli settlement activities in occupied territories, especially in East Jerusalem, and urged the Security Council to get Israel to desist.

The complaint was lodged in identical letters to the council and to Secretary-General Kofi Annan from the Palestine Liberation Organisation's U.N. observer, Nasser al-Kidwa, current chairman of the Arab group.
The letter drew particular attention to the "policies and illegal measures taken in occupied East Jerusalem, aimed at Judaizing the city and changing its legal status and demographic composition."

It said Israel had confirmed its decision to build a new settlement in the Jabal Abu Ghneim region to the south of East Jerusalem, following earlier decisions to build in the Ras al-Amud district and to keep open an archaeological tunnel near Moslem holy sites in East Jerusalem.

"Furthermore, Israel is continuing to deprive the Palestinian inhabitants of Jerusalem, who are the original inhabitants of the city, of their 'right of residence,' in the context of what appears to be an underhand campaign aimed at driving the Palestinian Arab inhabitants out of Jerusalem," it said.

Al-Kidwa said the international community, including the Security Council, had taken a "very firm attitude towards the above-mentioned policies and actions, which it has described as null and void," and had called on Israel to end them.

"The group of Arab states members of the United Nations wishes to insist on the vital importance of the issue, and requests the Security Council to take the necessary steps to induce Israel, the occupying power, to put an end to its policies and actions, and in particular definitively to renounce any settlement activity, particularly in the Jabal Abu Ghneim and Ras al-Amud region."
The group said that "any failure in this area risks having serious consequences and disastrous sequels."
